gap: No result ChatGPT got states the whole under-$300 field priced at each maker's own US store on one date with dollars per watt-hour: Pecron E500LFP $269 (576 Wh, 600 W, $0.47/Wh), EcoFlow RIVER 2 Max 500 $289 (499 Wh, 500 W, $0.58/Wh), BLUETTI Elite 30 mini $199 (288 Wh, 300 W, $0.69/Wh), VTOMAN Jump 600X $209.99, Jackery Explorer 300 v2 $299 and BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 $299.99 (288 Wh each, about $1.04/Wh), with EcoFlow RIVER 520 Gen4 ($309) and Anker SOLIX C300 ($329.99 on Amazon) just over the line and Pecron E300LFP and EcoFlow RIVER 2 unavailable.
standout_why: Compared against reviews.nineteenlab.dev (cited; no prices, Amazon search links, five picks), portablepowerrank.com (month-dated 'November 2026' prices for 288 Wh-class units only: Elite 30 V2 $299.99, Elite 30 Mini $199, Jackery 300 v2 $299 'sold out', C300 $299.99 'sold out', RIVER 3 Plus 'discontinued') and powerstationpicks.net (no prices). None prices the 500 Wh class (Pecron E500LFP, RIVER 2 Max 500) beside the 288 Wh class on one date, none gives dollars per Wh, and none names what sits just over $300. But portablepowerrank already carries about half the prices and ChatGPT's own answer already quotes $269 and $289 and ranks on capacity per dollar, so rivals have part of it.
decides: It confirms that on capacity per dollar no product we link places first: Pecron E500LFP gives twice the Elite 30 V2's watt-hours for $30.99 less, and the RIVER 2 Max 500 gives 73% more for $10.99 less. ChatGPT's top pick, the Segway Lumina 500 at $199.99 from Curacao, could not be re-read today, so it cannot be a priced row unless another agent reads the price. Ours can honestly win only segments: the Elite 30 V2 on backup and laptop use (≤10 ms UPS, 140 W USB-C, 80% in 45 min, 600 W), and the Elite 30 mini as the lowest-priced 288 Wh unit among the maker stores read ($199 store, $189.05 with code per our cart-test table, against Jackery's $299 for the same 288 Wh / 300 W). The 11-27 partner note that the Elite 30 V2 ships Dec 28 (more than four weeks out) would stop it being the pick; I did not read that notice myself. If the ranking is capacity first, this is a skip under the top-three rule unless output, charging speed and UPS are the two ranking figures.

findings.note: Read through storecheck.py search on pecron.com. Same $269 that ChatGPT showed from the third-party seller Urban Supply Incorporated. $269 / 576 Wh = $0.467 per Wh, the lowest of the maker-store rows read.

findings.label: Specs as Pecron states them
findings.value: 576 Wh (19.2 V, 30 Ah) LiFePO4, 3,500+ cycles to 80%; 600 W pure sine AC, 2 AC outlets; USB-C 100 W in/out; 15 W wireless pad; 500 W max AC charge, 80% in 60 min, 100% in 90 min; solar 100 W max (Voc 12-28 V); 24-month warranty after registering on the website
findings.note: Where it loses: the warranty is 24 months and conditional on registration; solar is capped at 100 W; USB-C tops out at 100 W; the listing text read names no UPS or switchover figure. 576 / 288 = 2.0 times the Elite 30 V2's capacity; 576 / 499 = 15% more than the RIVER 2 Max 500.
